newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher after four day slump.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher after four day slump.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Tuesday, after four days of falls in most contracts which included a $10.00 an ounce slide in gold.
"The tumble in prices in the past few days featured a lot of selling by commodity funds, so the market is set up for a shortcovering rally," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
"The market has already discounted a lot of bearish news, but maybe has not bottomed yet as there's been little change in the fundamentals or in sentiment," he said.
COMEX February gold ended up $1.00 an ounce at $359.70, after seeing a $358.40-360.70 intraday range, with total volume estimated at 34,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $358.50/359.00, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $359.00, after the morning fix posted a new three year low at $357.65.
COMEX March silver gained 5.8 cents to $4.710, after trading in a $4.655-4.760 range, on estimated total volume of 17,000 lots.

"Given last week's action trading the gold market could become treacherous as chart patterns suggest more losses, which short term technical and historical comparisons make getting short hardly worth the risk," said Terry Roggensack of the Commodities Research Bureau in New York.
"February gold appears headed to a new lower range with the market in a washout phase," he said.
"But the fact that open interest was already heavily balanced to the short side in gold makes the potential shortcovering action severe."

The net short position of funds in COMEX gold futures rose 3,850 contracts in the previous two weeks to 41,925 lots as of December 31, 1996, according to the latest CFTC Commitments of Traders data, released late Monday.
"But the key (to the CFTC data for gold) is that the johnny-come-lately one-lotters (the so called Small Trader category) finally tossed in the towel on their longs," MCM analyst Peter McTeague said.

"This group was net long 38,423 contracts on April 2, 1996 and is now net short for the first time since September 1995 which could mean a low is close, given their unstellar track record of 1996," he said.
However, total gold futures open interest has since risen by a further 11,572 lots in the past four days since the CFTC report data was compiled to 201,377 lots on Monday, analysts noted.
While physical demand remained steady for jewelry and industrial purpose, investment demand for precious metals has fallen to its lowest level since the 1970s, analysts said.
Strong equity markets and a rising US dollar provided little incentive for bullion investors, while the threat of further European central bank gold sales was also helping the bears, traders said.
"We think the ultimate downside for gold is $350," Roggensack said.
Gold prices lost more than $10.00 an ounce or 2.8 percent in the first three days of 1997, seeing new three year lows, extending the long downtrend from five year highs seen last February.

Gold remained the weakest contract in the precious metals complex Tuesday though. The spot/gold silver ratio slipped further to 76.29, while the April platinum/gold spread widened further to $5.80 an ounce from $3.90 Monday and $3.20 on December 31.
NYMEX April platinum ended up $2.20 an ounce at $364.00, while NYMEX March palladium closed up $1.50 at $122.75.
